options.B: No; strictly prohibited under Georgia statutory law and Board rules
options.C: No, unless specifically authorized under an emergency judicial order
options.D: Only if the psychologist has completed a minimum of two years of postdoctoral experience

explanation: Yes; they apply to all licensees and applicants, including conduct during required education/training/employment. (Rule 510-5-.01)

question_text: Who is the client when a corporation is the contracting party?

options.A: Nature/anticipated course of therapy, fees, third parties, limits of confidentiality
options.B: The organization, unless a separate professional relationship with an individual exists
options.C: Role, who is the client, probable uses of information, and limits of confidentiality
options.D: Refrain from the role if it could impair objectivity or expose others to harm/exploitation

explanation: The organization, unless a separate professional relationship with an individual exists. (Rule 510-5-.02)

question_text: What is 'telepsychology' in Georgia rules?

options.A: Unique concerns: technology used, boundaries, response procedures, risks
options.B: Correct via correction, retraction, erratum, or other appropriate means
options.C: Provision of psychological services using telecommunication technologies
options.D: Obtain sufficient training to ensure competence and engage in consultation

explanation: Provision of psychological services using telecommunication technologies. (Rule 510-5-.02)

question_text: What is required to practice telepsychology in Georgia?

options.A: Take reasonable steps to correct or minimize the misuse
options.B: Within 72 hours after receiving the certificate or order
options.C: Live online interactive video conferences in real time
options.D: Current active Georgia license or PSYPACT authorization

explanation: Current active Georgia license or PSYPACT authorization. (Rule 510-5-.07)

question_text: Must telepsychology meet the same standards as in-person services?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No; this constitutes an unwaivable conflict of interest under Board ethics rules
options.C: No; requires prior formal peer review and clearance by the Board ethics committee
options.D: No, unless the Board waives the requirement upon formal written application

question_text: What PSYPACT credentials allow interjurisdictional telepsychology?

options.A: The supervising psychologist personally
options.B: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization
options.C: Maximum 10 per course, 20 per biennium
options.D: Maximum 5 per article, 10 per biennium

explanation: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization. (Rule 510-5-.07)

question_text: How often must IPC and TAP be renewed under PSYPACT?

options.A: 48 hours
options.B: 72 hours
options.C: Annually
options.D: I/O fellows

explanation: Annually. (Rule 510-9-.03)

question_text: What must a psychologist do when impaired and in a professional relationship?

options.A: Licensed psychology, medicine (psychiatry/neurology/relevant medical field)
options.B: Obtain sufficient training to ensure competence and engage in consultation
options.C: Unique concerns: technology used, boundaries, response procedures, risks
options.D: Terminate appropriately, notify client in writing, and assist with referral

explanation: Terminate appropriately, notify client in writing, and assist with referral. (Rule 510-5-.05)

question_text: What may the Board require of an impaired licensee?

options.A: Exam, records, referral to Colleague Assistance Program, rehabilitation, practice restrictions
options.B: Consult knowledgeable colleagues, state/national ethics committees, or appropriate authorities
options.C: License application, examinations, billing, services, reports, and any other practice activity
options.D: Make known commitment to Ethics Code and attempt to resolve; if unresolvable, may follow law

explanation: Exam, records, referral to Colleague Assistance Program, rehabilitation, practice restrictions. (Rule 510-5-.05)

question_text: What happens if an impaired licensee refuses evaluation/rehabilitation?

options.A: Maximum 6 per biennium for two 3-hour workshops
options.B: May constitute basis for disciplinary sanctions
options.C: Two from health service providers in psychology
options.D: Maximum 12 per biennium for two 6-hour workshops

explanation: May constitute basis for disciplinary sanctions. (Rule 510-5-.05)

question_text: How long must adult psychological records be maintained?

options.A: One year after the last date of service
options.B: Two years after the last date of service
options.C: Seven years after the last date of service
options.D: Three years after the last date of service

explanation: Seven years after the last date of service. (Rule 510-5-.04)

question_text: How long must minor records be maintained?

options.A: Until one year after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later
options.B: Until two years after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later
options.C: Until four years after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later
options.D: Until three years after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later

explanation: Until three years after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later. (Rule 510-5-.04)

question_text: What must records include?

options.A: Identifying/contact data, fees/billing, informed consent, diagnosis/basis, plan, dates/services, interventions, assessment
options.B: To facilitate later services, replicate research, meet institutional requirements, ensure accurate billing, comply with law
options.C: Until three years after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later
options.D: Only if it is not clinically contraindicated and the resulting arrangement is not exploitative

explanation: Identifying/contact data, fees/billing, informed consent, diagnosis/basis, plan, dates/services, interventions, assessment. (Rule 510-5-.04)

question_text: What must psychologists do with records after termination?

options.A: Limited to the minimum necessary to achieve the purpose
options.B: Continue to treat client information as confidential
options.C: Risks to privacy and limits of confidentiality
options.D: Only information germane to the purpose of the communication

explanation: Continue to treat client information as confidential. (Rule 510-5-.06)

question_text: How many supervision hours are required per 20 hours of face-to-face clinical contact?

options.A: At least one-half
options.B: 40 per biennium
options.C: Minimum one hour
options.D: No more than three

explanation: Minimum one hour. (Rule 510-5-.06)

question_text: How many supervisees may a psychologist supervise concurrently without Board approval?

options.A: No more than two
options.B: No more than four
options.C: No more than five
options.D: No more than three

explanation: No more than three. (Rule 510-5-.06)

question_text: Who must make the diagnosis when clinical services are rendered by a supervisee?

options.A: The supervising psychologist personally
options.B: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization
options.C: Maximum 10 per course, 20 per biennium
options.D: Maximum 5 per article, 10 per biennium

explanation: The supervising psychologist personally. (Rule 510-5-.06)

question_text: Who may select and interpret psychological tests in a supervisory setting?

options.A: The psychologist
options.B: The psychologist only
options.C: The judge
options.D: Only as required by law or court order

explanation: The psychologist only. (Rule 510-5-.06)

question_text: Must a supervisee inform clients of their role and right to speak with the supervisor?

options.A: No, unless approved by a two-thirds majority of the Georgia State Board
options.B: Only when practicing under the direct supervision of a licensed physician or psychiatrist
options.C: Yes
options.D: Only if full written disclosure is provided to and countersigned by the client in advance

question_text: Who is responsible for supervisees' professional acts?

options.A: Persons are competent, have no exploitative multiple relationship, and perform competently
options.B: Attempt informal resolution with the individual if appropriate and confidentiality permits
options.C: Obtain consultation/assistance and determine whether to limit, suspend, or terminate duties
options.D: The supervising psychologist retains full, complete, ultimate authority and responsibility

explanation: The supervising psychologist retains full, complete, ultimate authority and responsibility. (Rule 510-5-.06)

question_text: Must a forensic psychologist personally examine the individual before testifying about psychological characteristics?

options.A: Yes, unless examination is not feasible; then limit conclusions
options.B: No; this constitutes an unwaivable conflict of interest under Board ethics rules
options.C: Only in inpatient psychiatric facilities or hospitals accredited by JCAHO
options.D: No, unless approved by a two-thirds majority of the Georgia State Board

explanation: Yes, unless examination is not feasible; then limit conclusions. (Rule 510-5-.08)

question_text: What standard governs court-appointed custody psychologists' good faith?

options.A: Make reasonable efforts to maintain integrity and security consistent with law
options.B: APA's 2010 Guidelines for Child Custody Evaluations in Family Law Proceedings
options.C: Manuals, instruments, protocols, and test questions/stimuli; excludes test data
options.D: Truthfully, honestly, candidly, and fairly describe the basis for testimony

explanation: APA's 2010 Guidelines for Child Custody Evaluations in Family Law Proceedings. (Rule 510-5-.08)

question_text: Who determines whether a court-appointed custody psychologist acted in bad faith?

options.A: The psychologist
options.B: The psychologist only
options.C: The judge
options.D: Only as required by law or court order

explanation: The judge. (Rule 510-5-.08)

question_text: May a Georgia psychologist supervise someone who surrendered a license due to discipline?

options.A: Yes, for temporary practice not exceeding 30 calendar days per calendar year
options.B: Yes, after a mandatory waiting period of two years following service termination
options.C: Yes, at the independent clinical discretion of the licensed psychologist
options.D: No, unless Board waives/modifies for extraordinary circumstances

explanation: No, unless Board waives/modifies for extraordinary circumstances. (Rule 510-5-.10)

question_text: Is failure to cooperate with a Board/national investigation a violation?

options.A: Yes
options.B: Only if the psychologist has completed a minimum of two years of postdoctoral experience
options.C: No, unless the Board waives the requirement upon formal written application
options.D: Only in inpatient psychiatric facilities or hospitals accredited by JCAHO

question_text: How many days before limited practice must an out-of-state psychologist notify the Board?

options.A: At least 10 days
options.B: At least 5 days
options.C: At least 14 days
options.D: At least 15 days

explanation: At least 5 days. (Rule 510-9-.03)

question_text: What is the maximum days per calendar year for limited practice in Georgia?

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 45 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 14 days

question_text: What disaster response networks are exempt from Georgia licensure?

options.A: When under direct supervision and responsibility of a licensed psychologist, without representing themselves as psychologists
options.B: Fraud/deception in applying or passing exam; felony conviction; false/assumed name; habitual intemperance; negligence; violation of 43-1-19
options.C: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.D: American Red Cross, ICISF, APA/Georgia Psychological Association Disaster Response Network, or other nationally recognized networks

explanation: American Red Cross, ICISF, APA/Georgia Psychological Association Disaster Response Network, or other nationally recognized networks. (Rule 510-9-.03)

question_text: What credentials are needed for temporary in-person practice under PSYPACT?

options.A: ASPPB IPC and PSYPACT TAP
options.B: Licensure by endorsement
options.C: Reserved (repealed 1986)
options.D: Not less than three months

explanation: ASPPB IPC and PSYPACT TAP. (Rule 510-9-.03)

question_text: How many days per year may PSYPACT psychologists practice temporarily in Georgia?

options.A: Up to 15 days per calendar year
options.B: Up to 30 days per calendar year
options.C: Up to 45 days per calendar year
options.D: Up to 14 days per calendar year

explanation: Up to 30 days per calendar year. (Rule 510-9-.03)

question_text: May an unlicensed person render psychological services for a fee?

options.A: Yes, if approved by a majority vote of the Georgia State Board of Examiners
options.B: Yes, if authorized under an explicit court order or judicial subpoena
options.C: No
options.D: Yes, under the physician-psychologist collaborative practice exception

question_text: May an unlicensed person supervise psychological services?

options.A: Yes, provided the arrangement is documented in writing and is not clinically contraindicated
options.B: Yes, provided all identifying client information is completely redacted or disguised
options.C: Yes, under the physician-psychologist collaborative practice exception
options.D: No

question_text: May an unlicensed person use titles implying licensure?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes, if conducted under the direct supervision of a Board-approved licensed psychologist
options.C: Yes, upon formal written petition and prior approval by the Georgia State Board
options.D: Yes, provided notice is given to the Secretary of State within 14 calendar days

question_text: Who may administer and interpret psychological tests?

options.A: Satisfy statutory/rule requirements and be under direct supervision of licensed psychologist
options.B: Currently licensed Georgia psychologist; students/trainees under direct licensed supervision
options.C: Raw and scaled scores, client responses, and psychologist notes/recordings during examination
options.D: Avoid multiple/conflicting roles; if unavoidable, clarify role expectations and confidentiality

explanation: Currently licensed Georgia psychologist; students/trainees under direct licensed supervision. (Rule 510-10-.03)

question_text: After how many failed EPPP attempts must additional coursework be completed?

options.A: Active duty or separation leave within 24 months of retirement or 12 months of separation
options.B: Doctoral degree from an APA/CPA accredited program in applied psychology (or equivalent)
options.C: After three unsuccessful attempts, 3 semester hours or 15 CE hours before 4th-6th retakes
options.D: Superior court of the county where the division director maintains offices (Fulton County)

explanation: After three unsuccessful attempts, 3 semester hours or 15 CE hours before 4th-6th retakes. (Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: After how many failed EPPP attempts are 9 semester hours required?

options.A: Up to 30 days per calendar year
options.B: Scheduled for a Full Board Exam
options.C: Practice psychology in Georgia
options.D: After six unsuccessful attempts

explanation: After six unsuccessful attempts. (Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: How long is an application valid after Board approval?

options.A: One year from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE
options.B: Two years from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE
options.C: Three years from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE
options.D: Four years from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE

explanation: One year from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE. (Rule 510-2-.06)

question_text: When may the Jurisprudence exam be scheduled?

options.A: Identified or clearly recognizable as paid advertisements
options.B: After passing the national exam and while completing SWE
options.C: Submit application for reinstatement per Rule 510-7-.02
options.D: Application, 40 CE hours within two years, and penalty fee

explanation: After passing the national exam and while completing SWE. (Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: When may the oral exam be scheduled?

options.A: After passing all exams and within 3 months of completing SWE
options.B: After passing all exams and within 6 months of completing SWE
options.C: After passing all exams and within 2 months of completing SWE
options.D: After passing all exams and within 11 months of completing SWE

explanation: After passing all exams and within 2 months of completing SWE. (Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: How recent must the oral exam work sample be?

options.A: Generated within 3 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice
options.B: Generated within 11 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice
options.C: Generated within 12 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice
options.D: Generated within 6 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice

explanation: Generated within 6 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice. (Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: What is the maximum CE credits per biennium for Area I (Academic)?

options.D: None

question_text: What is the minimum and maximum CE credits for Area II (Group Consultation)?

options.A: No more than 20% of internship/SWE
options.B: Minimum 10, maximum 20 per biennium
options.C: Not necessarily for clinical work
options.D: Maximum 10 per course, 20 per biennium

explanation: Minimum 10, maximum 20 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: What is the maximum CE credits for Area III (Approved Sponsored CE)?

options.A: Minimum one hour
options.B: At least one-half
options.C: 40 per biennium
options.D: No more than three

explanation: 40 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: How many psychologists must be in a group consultation group?

options.A: 6 credits, in-person or synchronous webinar
options.B: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization
options.C: The supervising psychologist personally
options.D: Minimum 3, maximum 8 licensed participants

explanation: Minimum 3, maximum 8 licensed participants. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: How many ethics CE credits are awarded for a full biennium of Georgia Psychological Association Ethics Committee service?

options.D: None

question_text: What satisfies all CE requirements in a biennium?

options.A: Initiating activities with substantial likelihood of impairment
options.B: Passing the American Board of Professional Psychology examination
options.C: Current Georgia or equivalent license; not under disciplinary order
options.D: The independent contractor, not under supervisory relationship

explanation: Passing the American Board of Professional Psychology examination. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: Who may bring an action to enjoin unlicensed practice generally?

options.A: Drug abuse treatment and education program approved by licensing authority
options.B: Mental/physical exam by Board-designated practitioner; production of records
options.C: The licensing board, division director, or appropriate prosecuting attorney
options.D: Minimum 3 full-time academic years plus internship before doctoral degree

explanation: The licensing board, division director, or appropriate prosecuting attorney. (OCGA 43-1-20)

question_text: Where is an unlicensed practice injunction action filed?

options.A: Office of State Administrative Hearings (OSAH)
options.B: Georgia Court of Appeals
options.C: Probate Court of the county of practice
options.D: Superior court of the county where the unlicensed person resides

explanation: Superior court of the county where the unlicensed person resides. (OCGA 43-1-20)

question_text: May the division director disclose information about pending investigations to other licensing authorities?

options.A: Yes, to any lawful licensing authority upon inquiry
options.B: Only with prior written authorization and credentialing from the Georgia State Board
options.C: No; strictly prohibited under Georgia statutory law and Board rules
options.D: No; this constitutes an unwaivable conflict of interest under Board ethics rules

explanation: Yes, to any lawful licensing authority upon inquiry. (OCGA 43-1-21)

question_text: Can the division director disclose investigations of unlicensed persons?

options.A: No, unless specifically authorized under an emergency judicial order
options.B: Yes, nothing prohibits disclosure of existence of unlicensed-practice investigations
options.C: Only with prior written authorization and credentialing from the Georgia State Board
options.D: No, unless approved by a two-thirds majority of the Georgia State Board

explanation: Yes, nothing prohibits disclosure of existence of unlicensed-practice investigations. (OCGA 43-1-21)

question_text: Are licensees required to file licenses with the clerk of superior court?

options.A: Yes, provided all identifying client information is completely redacted or disguised
options.B: Yes, with advance written notification to the Board and client waiver of privilege
options.C: No
options.D: Yes, for temporary practice not exceeding 30 calendar days per calendar year

question_text: Does forming a business entity exempt a professional from board regulation?

options.A: Yes, in emergency situations where failure to act poses imminent danger to life or safety
options.B: Yes, if authorized under an explicit court order or judicial subpoena
options.C: Yes, after a mandatory waiting period of two years following service termination
options.D: No; professionals remain subject to board regulation, including privilege and liability standards

explanation: No; professionals remain subject to board regulation, including privilege and liability standards. (OCGA 43-1-24)

question_text: May professional licensing boards promulgate rules to implement general provisions?

options.A: Yes
options.B: Only in inpatient psychiatric facilities or hospitals accredited by JCAHO
options.C: Only with prior written authorization and credentialing from the Georgia State Board
options.D: No, unless approved by a two-thirds majority of the Georgia State Board

explanation: Yes. (OCGA 43-1-25)

question_text: What must the board adopt and affix to licenses?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: A seal
options.C: ASPPB
options.D: 31 days

explanation: A seal. (OCGA 43-39-5)

question_text: What authority does the board have regarding codes of conduct?

options.A: Minimum; boards may impose more stringent sanctions
options.B: Fine $100-$1,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months
options.C: Authority to establish a code of conduct and ethics
options.D: Five years, serving until successors are appointed

explanation: Authority to establish a code of conduct and ethics. (OCGA 43-39-6)

question_text: What must board members do before entering office?

options.A: Current therapy clients/patients or vulnerable persons
options.B: 24 months unless Board grants exception; non-renewable
options.C: Submit application for reinstatement per Rule 510-7-.02
options.D: Take constitutional oath and file it with the Governor

explanation: Take constitutional oath and file it with the Governor. (OCGA 43-39-4)

question_text: For what reasons may board members be removed?

options.A: Incompetence, neglect of duty, malfeasance, or crime involving moral turpitude
options.B: Anyone holding any state-issued license/permit/certification for an occupation
options.C: County where the person resides or where corporation maintains principal office
options.D: Acts violating Board Code of Ethics or Code of Conduct, including by supervisees

explanation: Incompetence, neglect of duty, malfeasance, or crime involving moral turpitude. (OCGA 43-39-3)

question_text: Does licensure by reciprocity require Georgia standards not be lowered?

options.A: Only when practicing under the direct supervision of a licensed physician or psychiatrist
options.B: Yes; board may require additional examinations
options.C: No, unless approved by a two-thirds majority of the Georgia State Board
options.D: No; this constitutes an unwaivable conflict of interest under Board ethics rules

explanation: Yes; board may require additional examinations. (OCGA 43-39-10)

question_text: Are application fees refundable?

options.A: Yes, if conducted under the direct supervision of a Board-approved licensed psychologist
options.B: Yes, after a mandatory waiting period of two years following service termination
options.C: No; application and processing fees are non-refundable
options.D: Yes, provided notice is given to the Secretary of State within 14 calendar days

explanation: No; application and processing fees are non-refundable. (Rule 510-1-.05; Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: Within what time must a refund request of other fees be made?

options.A: Within two years of fee receipt
options.B: Within three years of fee receipt
options.C: Within four years of fee receipt
options.D: Within one year of fee receipt

explanation: Within one year of fee receipt. (Rule 510-1-.05)

question_text: How should Georgia's child abuse reporting law be construed?

options.A: Liberally, to carry out its protective purpose
options.B: Written or oral consent, permission, and assent
options.C: Inform affected individuals/groups at the outset
options.D: The student, except under exceptional circumstances

explanation: Liberally, to carry out its protective purpose. (OCGA 19-7-5)

question_text: What is the minimum period for failure to communicate/visit/support to show abandonment?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Six months
options.C: The psychologist
options.D: At least two years

explanation: Six months. (OCGA 19-7-5)

question_text: How long after a child is found without identification must a parent come forward to avoid abandonment?

options.A: Six months
options.B: The psychologist
options.C: Three months
options.D: At least two years

explanation: Three months. (OCGA 19-7-5)

question_text: What type of abuse triggers mandatory reporting for disabled adults/elders?

options.A: Only in specified low-risk settings or where permitted by law
options.B: Another appropriate professional to deal with emergency needs
options.C: Harassment/demeaning behavior based on protected characteristics
options.D: Abuse other than by accidental means, neglect, or exploitation

explanation: Abuse other than by accidental means, neglect, or exploitation. (OCGA 30-5-4)

question_text: Are clergy mandatory reporters of disabled adult/elder abuse?

options.A: Yes
options.B: Only during a declared state of public health emergency by the Governor
options.C: No; requires prior formal peer review and clearance by the Board ethics committee
options.D: Only if full written disclosure is provided to and countersigned by the client in advance

explanation: Yes. (OCGA 30-5-4)

question_text: Are financial institution employees mandatory reporters of elder exploitation?

options.A: Only for endorsement applicants with at least ten years of continuous active licensure
options.B: Yes, but not while acting as fiduciary for assets held in that capacity
options.C: Only with prior written authorization and credentialing from the Georgia State Board
options.D: No, unless the Board waives the requirement upon formal written application

explanation: Yes, but not while acting as fiduciary for assets held in that capacity. (OCGA 30-5-4)

question_text: If a mandated reporter works in a facility, who makes the report?

options.A: Any other person with reasonable cause to believe abuse/neglect/exploitation
options.B: Best interests of clients/patients, with consent and subject to law/contract
options.C: The staff person notifies the person in charge or designee, who then reports
options.D: Contact involving intimate parts of either person for sexual gratification

explanation: The staff person notifies the person in charge or designee, who then reports. (OCGA 30-5-4)

question_text: Can a health service provider psychologist order medications?

options.A: Yes, provided notice is given to the Secretary of State within 14 calendar days
options.B: Yes, if approved by a majority vote of the Georgia State Board of Examiners
options.C: Yes, for temporary practice not exceeding 30 calendar days per calendar year
options.D: No; psychologist's order excludes prescribing medications

explanation: No; psychologist's order excludes prescribing medications. (OCGA 31-7-160)

question_text: Can a health service provider psychologist order nursing assessments?

options.A: No; excluded from psychologist's order
options.B: Yes, under the physician-psychologist collaborative practice exception
options.C: Yes, upon formal written petition and prior approval by the Georgia State Board
options.D: Yes, for temporary practice not exceeding 30 calendar days per calendar year

explanation: No; excluded from psychologist's order. (OCGA 31-7-160)

question_text: Can a health service provider psychologist order medical procedures?

options.A: Yes, at the independent clinical discretion of the licensed psychologist
options.B: No; excluded from psychologist's order
options.C: Yes, after a mandatory waiting period of two years following service termination
options.D: Yes, if approved by a majority vote of the Georgia State Board of Examiners

explanation: No; excluded from psychologist's order. (OCGA 31-7-160)

question_text: May psychologists serve on hospital medical/professional staff committees?

options.A: No, unless approved by a two-thirds majority of the Georgia State Board
options.B: No; strictly prohibited under Georgia statutory law and Board rules
options.C: Yes, consistent with licensure and competence
options.D: No; requires prior formal peer review and clearance by the Board ethics committee

question_text: Does prior hospital staff membership protect current employment?

options.A: Only if full written disclosure is provided to and countersigned by the client in advance
options.B: No; this constitutes an unwaivable conflict of interest under Board ethics rules
options.C: No, unless approved by a two-thirds majority of the Georgia State Board
options.D: Yes; existing hospital staff psychologists may continue working

question_text: May hospital privileges be limited for nondiscriminatory rule violations?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No, unless the Board waives the requirement upon formal written application
options.C: Only if full written disclosure is provided to and countersigned by the client in advance
options.D: Only when practicing under the direct supervision of a licensed physician or psychiatrist

question_text: What does 'convicted' mean for licensed-person drug sanctions?

options.A: Verification from jurisdiction showing no disciplinary history
options.B: Final conviction, guilty/nolo plea, or first offender treatment
options.C: Practice psychology or use the title 'psychologist' in Georgia
options.D: License will not be renewed; may obtain credits within 31 days

question_text: What is a 'licensed individual' under OCGA 16-13-110?

options.A: Incompetence, neglect of duty, malfeasance, or crime involving moral turpitude
options.B: County where the person resides or where corporation maintains principal office
options.C: Anyone holding any state-issued license/permit/certification for an occupation
options.D: Acts violating Board Code of Ethics or Code of Conduct, including by supervisees

explanation: Anyone holding any state-issued license/permit/certification for an occupation. (OCGA 16-13-110)

question_text: Does the drug-sanction article apply to attorneys?

options.A: No, unless approved by a two-thirds majority of the Georgia State Board
options.B: Only in inpatient psychiatric facilities or hospitals accredited by JCAHO
options.C: Only if the psychologist has completed a minimum of two years of postdoctoral experience
options.D: Yes; practice of law is a licensed occupation and Supreme Court is licensing authority

explanation: Yes; practice of law is a licensed occupation and Supreme Court is licensing authority. (OCGA 16-13-110)

question_text: What accreditation must doctoral training programs have for Georgia licensure?

options.A: APA or CPA accreditation (with exceptions for I/O and international)
options.B: The Georgia Administrative Procedure Act (OCGA Title 50, Chapter 13)
options.C: Chapter 295-3 through 295-13 of the Office of Joint Secretary rules
options.D: Refuse to grant, revoke, discipline, or impose probationary license

explanation: APA or CPA accreditation (with exceptions for I/O and international). (Rule 510-2-.04)

question_text: How many full-time academic years of graduate study are required?

options.A: Three years at least 30 hours/week for 50 weeks/year in organized setting

options.B: Practice psychology or use the title 'psychologist' in Georgia
options.C: Verification from jurisdiction showing no disciplinary history
options.D: After passing all exams and within 2 months of completing SWE

explanation: Practice psychology or use the title 'psychologist' in Georgia. (Rule 510-7-.03)

question_text: How does a licensee reactivate inactive status?

options.A: Take constitutional oath and file it with the Governor
options.B: After passing the national exam and while completing SWE
options.C: Submit application for reinstatement per Rule 510-7-.02
options.D: 24 months unless Board grants exception; non-renewable

explanation: Submit application for reinstatement per Rule 510-7-.02. (Rule 510-7-.03)

question_text: What does 'synchronous' CE mean?

options.A: Current active Georgia license or PSYPACT authorization
options.B: A substantial portion must be in an inpatient setting
options.C: Take reasonable steps to correct or minimize the misuse
options.D: Live online interactive video conferences in real time

explanation: Live online interactive video conferences in real time. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: What does 'asynchronous' CE mean?

options.A: Online courses or recordings accessed on one's own schedule
options.B: Official certificate with date, title, location, and hours
options.C: One hour, during the week of service or the following week
options.D: 20 hours in the two years immediately prior to application

explanation: Online courses or recordings accessed on one's own schedule. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: How many CE credits for first/second authoring a peer-reviewed article?

options.A: Maximum 10 per course, 20 per biennium
options.B: Maximum 5 per article, 10 per biennium
options.C: The supervising psychologist personally
options.D: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization

explanation: Maximum 5 per article, 10 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: How many CE credits for teaching a semester course for the first time?

options.A: Maximum 5 per article, 10 per biennium
options.B: The supervising psychologist personally
options.C: Maximum 10 per course, 20 per biennium
options.D: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization

explanation: Maximum 10 per course, 20 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: How many CE credits for first-time 6-hour workshop presentation?

options.A: Established scientific and professional knowledge
options.B: Maximum 6 per biennium for two 3-hour workshops
options.C: May constitute basis for disciplinary sanctions
options.D: Maximum 12 per biennium for two 6-hour workshops

explanation: Maximum 12 per biennium for two 6-hour workshops. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: How many CE credits for first-time 3-hour workshop presentation?

options.A: Maximum 6 per biennium for two 3-hour workshops
options.B: May constitute basis for disciplinary sanctions
options.C: Two from health service providers in psychology
options.D: 40 credits, including 6 in professional ethics

explanation: Maximum 6 per biennium for two 3-hour workshops. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: What is the maximum academic course CE credits per biennium?
What is the maximum group consultation CE credits per biennium?
How many ethics CE credits for serving as a Board oral exam subcommittee member per day?

options.A: 20 credits, including 3 ethics
options.B: Not necessarily for clinical work
options.C: No more than 20% of internship/SWE
options.D: 3 per day, up to 6 per biennium

explanation: 3 per day, up to 6 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: How many ethics CE credits for completing a Board peer review with written report?

options.A: 3 for current biennium
options.B: At least one year prior
options.C: Chapters 510-4 and 510-5
options.D: At least two persons

explanation: 3 for current biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: What must CE documentation for approved sponsor activities include?

options.A: In person or real-time face-to-face video teleconferencing
options.B: Official certificate with date, title, location, and hours
options.C: 20 hours in the two years immediately prior to application
options.D: One hour, during the week of service or the following week

explanation: Official certificate with date, title, location, and hours. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: Who is eligible for a temporary license?

options.A: Majority of the entire board
options.B: Not less than three months
options.C: Only endorsement applicants
options.D: ASPPB IPC and PSYPACT TAP

explanation: Only endorsement applicants. (Rule 510-9-.01)

question_text: What exams must an endorsement applicant pass for a temporary license?

options.A: The Georgia Board oral examination
options.B: CPCCC (Comprehensive Psychology Competency Exam)
options.C: ABPP Specialty Board Examination
options.D: EPPP and Georgia Jurisprudence, and be eligible for oral exam

explanation: EPPP and Georgia Jurisprudence, and be eligible for oral exam. (Rule 510-9-.01)

question_text: How long may a temporary license holder continue to practice without full endorsement?

options.A: Maximum 12 months
options.B: Maximum 11 months
options.C: Maximum 6 months
options.D: Maximum 18 months

explanation: Maximum 12 months. (Rule 510-9-.01)

question_text: Who may receive a provisional license?

options.A: Statements must be based on professional knowledge and not imply a professional relationship
options.B: Someone who passed all written exams and completed all requirements except SWE and oral exam
options.C: ASPPB Certificate of Professional Qualification holders who pass jurisprudence and oral exams
options.D: Sanctions/discipline by any lawful authority; voluntary surrender of any psychology license

explanation: Someone who passed all written exams and completed all requirements except SWE and oral exam. (Rule 510-9-.02)

question_text: Does a provisional license carry full privileges?

options.A: No, unless the Board waives the requirement upon formal written application
options.B: No, unless specifically authorized under an emergency judicial order
options.C: Yes, except continued supervision is required throughout SWE
options.D: No, unless approved by a two-thirds majority of the Georgia State Board

explanation: Yes, except continued supervision is required throughout SWE. (Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: Is provisional license revocation a contested case under the APA?

options.A: Yes, for temporary practice not exceeding 30 calendar days per calendar year
options.B: Yes, at the independent clinical discretion of the licensed psychologist
options.C: Yes, after a mandatory waiting period of two years following service termination
options.D: No, but holder has right to appear before Board

explanation: No, but holder has right to appear before Board. (Rule 510-9-.02)

question_text: For limited practice, what must the out-of-state psychologist submit?

options.A: Verification from jurisdiction showing no disciplinary history
options.B: Practice psychology or use the title 'psychologist' in Georgia
options.C: License will not be renewed; may obtain credits within 31 days
options.D: EPPP and Georgia Jurisprudence, and be eligible for oral exam

explanation: Verification from jurisdiction showing no disciplinary history. (Rule 510-9-.03)

question_text: What services may an unlicensed individual not render?

options.A: Division Director, Professional Licensing Boards Division, Office of Secretary of State
options.B: Any service involving application of psychological principles for fee or remuneration
options.C: Application, 40 CE hours, plus passing Georgia Jurisprudence and Oral Examinations
options.D: Doctoral degree from an APA/CPA accredited program in applied psychology (or equivalent)

explanation: Any service involving application of psychological principles for fee or remuneration. (Rule 510-10-.01)

question_text: May an unlicensed person advertise board licensure?

options.A: Yes, provided the arrangement is documented in writing and is not clinically contraindicated
options.B: Yes, if authorized under an explicit court order or judicial subpoena
options.C: No
options.D: Yes, under the physician-psychologist collaborative practice exception

question_text: May an unlicensed person use titles implying licensure?

options.A: Yes, with advance written notification to the Board and client waiver of privilege
options.B: Yes, provided notice is given to the Secretary of State within 14 calendar days
options.C: Yes, provided full written informed consent is documented in the client record
options.D: No

question_text: What is required for students/trainees to administer/interpret psychological tests?

options.A: Satisfy statutory/rule requirements and be under direct supervision of licensed psychologist
options.B: Currently licensed Georgia psychologist; students/trainees under direct licensed supervision
options.C: Raw and scaled scores, client responses, and psychologist notes/recordings during examination
options.D: Avoid multiple/conflicting roles; if unavoidable, clarify role expectations and confidentiality

explanation: Satisfy statutory/rule requirements and be under direct supervision of licensed psychologist. (Rule 510-10-.03)

question_text: Are educational/vocational/achievement tests exclusively within psychology?

options.A: Yes, provided notice is given to the Secretary of State within 14 calendar days
options.B: No; psychologists also administer them, but they are not solely psychology's domain
options.C: Yes, if authorized under an explicit court order or judicial subpoena
options.D: Yes, provided the arrangement is documented in writing and is not clinically contraindicated

explanation: No; psychologists also administer them, but they are not solely psychology's domain. (Rule 510-10-.03)

question_text: Who administers the Georgia psychology board?

options.A: Doctoral degree from an APA/CPA accredited program in applied psychology (or equivalent)
options.B: Any service involving application of psychological principles for fee or remuneration
options.C: Division Director, Professional Licensing Boards Division, Office of Secretary of State
options.D: After three unsuccessful attempts, 3 semester hours or 15 CE hours before 4th-6th retakes

explanation: Division Director, Professional Licensing Boards Division, Office of Secretary of State. (Rule 510-1-.03)

question_text: Under OCGA 19-7-5, what is the mandatory timeframe within which suspected child abuse must be reported?

options.A: Immediately, but in no case later than 12 hours from the time there is reasonable cause to believe suspected child abuse occurred
options.B: Immediately, but in no case later than 48 hours from the time there is reasonable cause to believe suspected child abuse occurred
options.C: Immediately, but in no case later than 72 hours from the time there is reasonable cause to believe suspected child abuse occurred
options.D: Immediately, but in no case later than 24 hours from the time there is reasonable cause to believe suspected child abuse occurred

explanation: Immediately, but in no case later than 24 hours from the time there is reasonable cause to believe suspected child abuse occurred. (OCGA 19-7-5(e))

question_text: To which agencies must a mandated report of suspected child abuse be made under Georgia law?

options.A: Child welfare agency (DFCS) of county where child resides or abuse occurred, or appropriate police authority or district attorney
options.B: Georgia Composite Medical Board
options.C: Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities
options.D: County Board of Health and Wellness

explanation: Child welfare agency (DFCS) of county where child resides or abuse occurred, or appropriate police authority or district attorney. (OCGA 19-7-5(e))

question_text: Does statutory or common law privilege excuse a psychologist from reporting suspected child abuse under OCGA 19-7-5?

options.A: Yes, provided full written informed consent is documented in the client record
options.B: No; child abuse must be reported notwithstanding any privileged communication, with the sole exception of clergy-penitent confession
options.C: Yes, if approved by a majority vote of the Georgia State Board of Examiners
options.D: Yes, for temporary practice not exceeding 30 calendar days per calendar year

explanation: No; child abuse must be reported notwithstanding any privileged communication, with the sole exception of clergy-penitent confession. (OCGA 19-7-5(g))

question_text: What is the criminal penalty for a mandated reporter who knowingly and willfully fails to report suspected child abuse?

options.A: 1,500 hours
options.B: At least 80%
options.C: Misdemeanor
options.D: The Governor

explanation: Misdemeanor. (OCGA 19-7-5(h))

question_text: What immunity is provided to a person who makes a report of suspected child abuse in good faith?

options.A: The division director under the board's seal
options.B: Lapsed; reinstatement is at Board discretion
options.C: A trainee title such as 'intern' or 'resident'
options.D: Immunity from any civil or criminal liability

explanation: Immunity from any civil or criminal liability. (OCGA 19-7-5(f))

question_text: Does a licensed psychologist have legal authority to execute a certificate for emergency involuntary mental health admission (Form 1013)?

options.A: Yes; under OCGA 37-3-41(d), a licensed psychologist may perform any act specified by the section to be performed by a physician, with equal legal authority
options.B: Only when practicing under the direct supervision of a licensed physician or psychiatrist
options.C: No, unless the Board waives the requirement upon formal written application
options.D: Only if the psychologist has completed a minimum of two years of postdoctoral experience

explanation: Yes; under OCGA 37-3-41(d), a licensed psychologist may perform any act specified by the section to be performed by a physician, with equal legal authority. (OCGA 37-3-41(d))

question_text: What must a peace officer execute when taking a person into custody and delivering them under OCGA 37-3-41?

options.A: Telepsychology must adhere to the exact same legal, ethical, and clinical standards as in-person psychological practice
options.B: A written report detailing apprehension circumstances, which becomes part of the clinical record with the certificate or court order
options.C: Order by a health service provider psychologist for care/treatment in a medical facility, excluding meds, nursing assessments, or medical procedures
options.D: Employee is subject to employer's direction of time, manner, and method; independent contractor controls those

explanation: A written report detailing apprehension circumstances, which becomes part of the clinical record with the certificate or court order. (OCGA 37-3-41(c))

question_text: Within what timeframe must a peace officer act to take a person into custody upon receiving a Form 1013 certificate or court order?

options.A: Within 48 hours after receiving the certificate or order
options.B: Within 96 hours after receiving the certificate or order
options.C: Within 72 hours after receiving the certificate or order
options.D: Within 24 hours after receiving the certificate or order

explanation: Within 72 hours after receiving the certificate or order. (OCGA 37-3-41(a),(b))

question_text: Is victim consent a defense to criminal prosecution for improper sexual contact by a psychotherapist under OCGA 16-6-5.1?

options.A: Yes, if authorized under an explicit court order or judicial subpoena
options.B: Yes, with advance written notification to the Board and client waiver of privilege
options.C: Yes, under the physician-psychologist collaborative practice exception
options.D: No; consent of the victim shall not be a defense to prosecution under this Code section

explanation: No; consent of the victim shall not be a defense to prosecution under this Code section. (OCGA 16-6-5.1(d))

question_text: What constitutes improper sexual contact by a psychotherapist in the first degree under OCGA 16-6-5.1?

options.A: Knowingly engaging in sexually explicit conduct with a person who is the subject of actual or purported psychotherapy treatment or counseling
options.B: Immediately, but in no case later than 24 hours from the time there is reasonable cause to believe suspected child abuse occurred
options.C: Child welfare agency (DFCS) of county where child resides or abuse occurred, or appropriate police authority or district attorney
options.D: An individual entrusted by agreement with a parent or guardian with the responsibility of education and supervision of a minor

explanation: Knowingly engaging in sexually explicit conduct with a person who is the subject of actual or purported psychotherapy treatment or counseling. (OCGA 16-6-5.1(b)(6))

question_text: What is the penalty for improper sexual contact by a psychotherapist in the first degree under OCGA 16-6-5.1?

options.A: Felony punishable by 1 to 25 years imprisonment and fine up to $250 (10 to 30 years if victim is under 16)
options.B: Felony punishable by 1 to 25 years imprisonment and fine up to $100,000 (10 to 30 years if victim is under 16)
options.C: Felony punishable by 1 to 25 years imprisonment and fine up to $500 (10 to 30 years if victim is under 16)
options.D: Felony punishable by 1 to 25 years imprisonment and fine up to $1,000 (10 to 30 years if victim is under 16)

explanation: Felony punishable by 1 to 25 years imprisonment and fine up to $100,000 (10 to 30 years if victim is under 16). (OCGA 16-6-5.1(f))

question_text: What constitutes improper sexual contact by a psychotherapist in the second degree, and what is its penalty?

options.A: Knowingly engaging in sexual contact (excluding sexually explicit conduct) with a psychotherapy client; punished as high and aggravated misdemeanor (felony 1-1 year on 2nd conviction)
options.B: Knowingly engaging in sexual contact (excluding sexually explicit conduct) with a psychotherapy client; punished as high and aggravated misdemeanor (felony 1-2 years on 2nd conviction)
options.C: Knowingly engaging in sexual contact (excluding sexually explicit conduct) with a psychotherapy client; punished as high and aggravated misdemeanor (felony 1-5 years on 2nd conviction)
options.D: Knowingly engaging in sexual contact (excluding sexually explicit conduct) with a psychotherapy client; punished as high and aggravated misdemeanor (felony 1-3 years on 2nd conviction)

explanation: Knowingly engaging in sexual contact (excluding sexually explicit conduct) with a psychotherapy client; punished as high and aggravated misdemeanor (felony 1-5 years on 2nd conviction). (OCGA 16-6-5.1(c)(6),(g))

question_text: Who is a 'person in a position of trust' under OCGA 16-6-5.1?

options.A: Sexual solicitation, advances, or verbal/nonverbal sexual conduct that is unwelcome/offensive or creates hostile environment
options.B: Child welfare agency (DFCS) of county where child resides or abuse occurred, or appropriate police authority or district attorney
options.C: Immediately, but in no case later than 24 hours from the time there is reasonable cause to believe suspected child abuse occurred
options.D: An individual entrusted by agreement with a parent or guardian with the responsibility of education and supervision of a minor

explanation: An individual entrusted by agreement with a parent or guardian with the responsibility of education and supervision of a minor. (OCGA 16-6-5.1(a)(5.1))

question_text: Does professional or statutory privilege prevent mandatory reporting of elder or disabled adult abuse under OCGA 30-5-4?

options.A: No; abuse, neglect, or exploitation must be reported notwithstanding any privileged communication (except clergy confession)
options.B: Yes, provided the arrangement is documented in writing and is not clinically contraindicated
options.C: Yes, provided notice is given to the Secretary of State within 14 calendar days
options.D: Yes, if approved by a majority vote of the Georgia State Board of Examiners

explanation: No; abuse, neglect, or exploitation must be reported notwithstanding any privileged communication (except clergy confession). (OCGA 30-5-4(d))

question_text: By what means may a report of suspected disabled adult or elder abuse be submitted under OCGA 30-5-4?

options.A: No more than three supervisees
options.B: Oral or written communication
options.C: Any person under 18 years of age
options.D: Equitable alternative activities

explanation: Oral or written communication. (OCGA 30-5-4(b)(2))

question_text: Within what timeframe must a law enforcement agency forward a report of elder or disabled adult abuse to the adult protection director?

options.A: Within 12 hours of receipt
options.B: Within 48 hours of receipt
options.C: Within 24 hours of receipt
options.D: Within 72 hours of receipt

explanation: Within 24 hours of receipt. (OCGA 30-5-4(b)(3))

question_text: Under OCGA 43-39-7(8), how many days per year may an out-of-state licensed psychologist practice in Georgia without a Georgia license?

options.A: No more than 1 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.B: No more than 2 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.C: No more than 3 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.D: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided

explanation: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided. (OCGA 43-39-7(8); Rule 510-9-.03)

question_text: Does an individual holding authority under PSYPACT need to apply for a Georgia license to practice telepsychology or temporary in-person practice in Georgia?

options.A: No; practicing pursuant to PSYPACT (Article 2 of Chapter 39) is an express statutory exception to Georgia licensure
options.B: Yes, provided full written informed consent is documented in the client record
options.C: Yes, with advance written notification to the Board and client waiver of privilege
options.D: Yes, if approved by a majority vote of the Georgia State Board of Examiners

explanation: No; practicing pursuant to PSYPACT (Article 2 of Chapter 39) is an express statutory exception to Georgia licensure. (OCGA 43-39-7(9))

question_text: Under what conditions may psychology students, trainees, or assistants engage in psychology activities without a license?

options.A: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.B: When under direct supervision and responsibility of a licensed psychologist, without representing themselves as psychologists
options.C: American Red Cross, ICISF, APA/Georgia Psychological Association Disaster Response Network, or other nationally recognized networks
options.D: Through subpoena by the division director upon reasonable grounds, and such records are admissible in board hearings

explanation: When under direct supervision and responsibility of a licensed psychologist, without representing themselves as psychologists. (OCGA 43-39-7(7))

question_text: Who regulates psychological testing and assessment performed by licensed professional counselors and social workers in Georgia?

options.A: Fraud/deception in applying or passing exam; felony conviction; false/assumed name; habitual intemperance; negligence; violation of 43-1-19
options.B: American Red Cross, ICISF, APA/Georgia Psychological Association Disaster Response Network, or other nationally recognized networks
options.C: The Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors, Social Workers, and Marriage and Family Therapists has sole authority under Chapter 10A
options.D: When under direct supervision and responsibility of a licensed psychologist, without representing themselves as psychologists

explanation: The Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors, Social Workers, and Marriage and Family Therapists has sole authority under Chapter 10A. (OCGA 43-39-7(10))

question_text: Does the statutory definition of the practice of psychology in Georgia permit psychologists to prescribe drugs or practice medicine?

options.A: Yes, under the physician-psychologist collaborative practice exception
options.B: Yes, upon formal written petition and prior approval by the Georgia State Board
options.C: Yes, if conducted under the direct supervision of a Board-approved licensed psychologist
options.D: No; nothing in the definition shall be construed as permitting administration or prescription of drugs or infringing upon practice of medicine

explanation: No; nothing in the definition shall be construed as permitting administration or prescription of drugs or infringing upon practice of medicine. (OCGA 43-39-1(7))

question_text: Can a psychologist's description of testing as 'psychological' in nature alter the statutory definition of psychological testing under OCGA 43-39-1(6)?

options.A: No; labeling cannot alter the statutory definition requiring measurement of mental abilities/personality/brain function and diagnosing disorders
options.B: Yes, provided notice is given to the Secretary of State within 14 calendar days
options.C: Yes, provided the arrangement is documented in writing and is not clinically contraindicated
options.D: Yes, provided full written informed consent is documented in the client record

explanation: No; labeling cannot alter the statutory definition requiring measurement of mental abilities/personality/brain function and diagnosing disorders. (OCGA 43-39-1(7))

question_text: Which Georgia statute governs Board hearings for license refusal, suspension, or revocation under OCGA 43-39-13?

options.A: APA or CPA accreditation (with exceptions for I/O and international)
options.B: The Georgia Administrative Procedure Act (OCGA Title 50, Chapter 13)
options.C: Chapter 295-3 through 295-13 of the Office of Joint Secretary rules
options.D: Refuse to grant, revoke, discipline, or impose probationary license

explanation: The Georgia Administrative Procedure Act (OCGA Title 50, Chapter 13). (OCGA 43-39-13(b))

question_text: Where must an appeal of a Board decision refusing, suspending, or revoking a license be filed?

options.A: Office of State Administrative Hearings (OSAH)
options.B: Georgia Court of Appeals
options.C: Superior court of the county where the division director maintains offices (Fulton County)
options.D: Probate Court of the county of practice

explanation: Superior court of the county where the division director maintains offices (Fulton County). (OCGA 43-39-13(c))

question_text: Under what standard of review must the superior court evaluate the Board's findings of fact on appeal?

options.A: Generated within 6 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice
options.B: Only those from regionally accredited institutions or that were the basis for psychology licensure
options.C: Assessment/diagnosis theories, effective treatment, consultation/supervision, evaluating efficacy
options.D: Any evidence standard: if findings are supported by any evidence, they must be accepted by the court

explanation: Any evidence standard: if findings are supported by any evidence, they must be accepted by the court. (OCGA 43-39-13(c))

question_text: What maximum civil fine may a Georgia professional licensing board impose per violation under OCGA 43-1-19?

options.A: A fine not to exceed $500.00 for each violation
options.B: A fine not to exceed $250.00 for each violation
options.C: A fine not to exceed $1,000.00 for each violation
options.D: A fine not to exceed $2,500.00 for each violation

explanation: A fine not to exceed $500.00 for each violation. (OCGA 43-1-19(d)(4))

question_text: Under OCGA 43-1-19, how may the Board obtain medical and mental health records of an applicant or licensee?

options.A: Individual differences, human development, dysfunctional behavior/psychopathology, ethics/professional standards
options.B: Through subpoena by the division director upon reasonable grounds, and such records are admissible in board hearings
options.C: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.D: Only uncompensated for public/nonprofit agencies serving indigent patients in underserved/critical-need areas

explanation: Through subpoena by the division director upon reasonable grounds, and such records are admissible in board hearings. (OCGA 43-1-19(c))

question_text: What is the effect of an adjudication of mental incompetence by a court on a psychologist's Georgia license?

options.A: Manufacture, distribution, trafficking, sale, or possession of controlled substance or marijuana
options.B: Biological, cognitive/affective, social, history/systems, measurement, methodology, data analysis
options.C: Automatic suspension of the license for as long as the adjudication of incompetence is in effect
options.D: Assessment/diagnosis theories, effective treatment, consultation/supervision, evaluating efficacy

explanation: Automatic suspension of the license for as long as the adjudication of incompetence is in effect. (OCGA 43-1-19(a)(9))

question_text: Does a sentence entered pursuant to a plea of nolo contendere or first-offender treatment constitute grounds for Board discipline under OCGA 43-1-19?

options.A: Only when practicing under the direct supervision of a licensed physician or psychiatrist
options.B: Only for endorsement applicants with at least ten years of continuous active licensure
options.C: Only if the psychologist has completed a minimum of two years of postdoctoral experience
options.D: Yes; both are conclusive evidence of an arrest and sentencing and constitute grounds for disciplinary sanction

explanation: Yes; both are conclusive evidence of an arrest and sentencing and constitute grounds for disciplinary sanction. (OCGA 43-1-19(a)(4))

question_text: What is the maximum number of supervisees for whom a psychologist may take primary supervisory responsibility without prior Board approval?

options.A: No more than three supervisees
options.B: No more than two supervisees
options.C: No more than four supervisees
options.D: No more than five supervisees

explanation: No more than three supervisees. (Rule 510-5-.06(3)(a)(5); Rule 510-2-.05)

question_text: What must a supervisee inform a client before providing psychological services?

options.A: Nature/procedures, risks/benefits, limits of confidentiality, fees, third parties, opportunity to ask questions
options.B: Supervisee status, supervisor name and contact info, and client right to confer with the supervising psychologist
options.C: Felony punishable by 1 to 25 years imprisonment and fine up to $100,000 (10 to 30 years if victim is under 16)
options.D: Purpose, duration, procedures, right to decline/withdraw, risks/benefits, confidentiality limits, incentives, contact

explanation: Supervisee status, supervisor name and contact info, and client right to confer with the supervising psychologist. (Rule 510-5-.06(3)(a)(4); Rule 510-2-.05)

question_text: May a psychologist withhold client records needed for emergency treatment solely because payment for services has not been received?

options.A: Yes, with advance written notification to the Board and client waiver of privilege
options.B: Yes, provided full written informed consent is documented in the client record
options.C: No; psychologists may not withhold records requested and needed for a client emergency treatment solely for nonpayment
options.D: Yes, after a mandatory waiting period of two years following service termination

explanation: No; psychologists may not withhold records requested and needed for a client emergency treatment solely for nonpayment. (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 6.03)

question_text: When is bartering for psychological services ethically permissible under Board rules?

options.A: Activities, total hours, client/patient involvement hours, and individual supervision hours
options.B: Advance plans to transfer records and protect confidentiality if withdrawing from practice
options.C: Until three years after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later
options.D: Only if it is not clinically contraindicated and the resulting arrangement is not exploitative

explanation: Only if it is not clinically contraindicated and the resulting arrangement is not exploitative. (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 6.05; Rule 510-5-.01)

question_text: What is required before recording the voices or images of clients to whom psychological services are provided?

options.A: Prior permission from the client or their legal representative
options.B: Only if disguised, consented in writing, or legally authorized
options.C: Take reasonable precautions to protect confidential information
options.D: Only information germane to the purpose of the communication

explanation: Prior permission from the client or their legal representative. (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 4.03)

question_text: What is the distinction between 'test data' and 'test materials' under APA Standard 9.04 and 9.11?

options.A: Use of assessment instruments to measure mental abilities, personality, or neuropsychological functioning and to diagnose/evaluate mental disorders
options.B: Test data includes raw/scaled scores, client responses, and notes; test materials refers to manuals, instruments, protocols, and test questions (which must be secured)
options.C: Information and techniques sufficient to substantiate findings, including personal interviews when appropriate
options.D: Purpose, test factors, test-taking abilities, situational/personal/linguistic/cultural differences

explanation: Test data includes raw/scaled scores, client responses, and notes; test materials refers to manuals, instruments, protocols, and test questions (which must be secured). (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 9.04, 9.11)

question_text: What professional standard applies to psychological services delivered via telecommunications technology in Georgia?
